subject: North Village District zoning/setbacks
comment: I have some concerns about the large developments proposed on 1600 W. and 400 N. 1. 1600 N is already very narrow and crowded as you go East to access 1-15. I'm concerned that we are adding more residents to an area that isn't equipped to handle the current traffic needs. I request that the 1600 N access to I-15 be widen with more lanes before we add more residents. 2. I'm concerned about the increase of traffic in residential neighborhoods. I request parking lot access to these developments be off State Street or where 1600 N is business zoned, not in residential neighborhoods like 400 N or west 1600 N. 3. I'm concerned about the proposed 6 story height of these developments so close to residential neighborhoods and by businesses that are single or two story structures. I request setbacks of 75 feet from residential homes and structure height lower as it approaches existing homes.

subject: general public comment
comment: We moved to Orem in 1969. To put that into perspective we moved here before they had a traffic signal light at the intersection of 1600 North and State Street. We have lived on 1600 North this entire time. We have watched a quiet country road turn into an extremely busy city street. We built our home on property that my Grandfather owned and farmed until his death, so it is meaningful to me, and is the main reason why we have stayed in Orem. When we wanted to build our home we were only able to do so, if we put in the sidewalk, curb and gutter along our property, and it had to be done at our expense. Later on the City put in the sidewalk, curb and gutter all along 1600 North at the Cities expense (our taxes) for all those who didn't have it. Then the street became so busy that the City had to come in on our frontage to widen the road, and they tore up my sidewalk without any consideration. That's not the end of the story! A second time they widened the road and again came in on our frontage. This time we were left without a pull over in front of our house. Our newspaper delivery person told us it was to dangerous for him to deliver the paper to us , and we would need to move our paper box. So after 50 years we stopped taking the newspaper. And now we have the City figuring to allow a development that will further frustrate the people who live in our area with even busier streets! There are certain times of the day when we can't get out of our driveway as it is! Sadly this is only one of the problematic issues we will be dealing with. Orem City, we have put up with a lot over the years since we have been here, but this one is just asking to much!

subject: North Village District zoning/setbacks
comment: I want to thank the city planning folks for making this recommendation. I am happy that the council passed the 75' setback. The residential rezone adds an additional setback to the height that will help preserve our privacy and somewhat of a neighborhood feel. The developer has rights to develop his property, and he purchased bottlenecked property with no real access to State street. Development should be pushed toward state street. He needs realistic plans for the property he purchased.
